name: Möja
description: Möja is an easy but distinctive SAT section: about 13.8 km of mostly gravel/local road walking from Långvik through Ramsmora, Löka, Berg and Möjaström to Hamn, then back to Berg where the main services are. It is not a full island loop, and Hamn has no ferry quay or services. Treat the route as a multi-access linear section through living archipelago villages, with Berg/Kyrkviken as the primary public-service cluster and several other villages/quays useful for shorter variants.
utilities: Confirmed public hiker-facing toilet at Berg/Kyrkviken guest harbour; SAT says not in winter.
Confirmed water at Berg/Kyrkviken guest harbour; SAT says not in winter. Iteration 2 added a possible fee/container-refill caveat.
Coop Berg is the strongest year-round food/shop service; opening/staffed-service details vary.
Coop Långvik exists but requires the Coop app plus Swedish BankID; do not expose as food/resupply unless the app supports conditional BankID-gated service notes.

Jeppes in Långvik, Möja Värdshus/Bageri, Les Poissonniers/Möja Fisk, Möja Hamnbar/Hamncafé and Möja Gästhem are useful food/cafe/lodging context when open, but hours are seasonal or verify-before-relying.
No official campsite, public SAT firepit or hiker shelter confirmed in iteration 1.
Guest-harbour toilets/water/showers outside Berg, paid/customer toilet/water and shower/sauna/gym services remain conditional/non-rendering metadata, not general public trail utilities.
Waste should default to pack-out guidance. Municipal waste/recycling infrastructure, including Möja ÅVC/recycling, and harbour waste should not be rendered as normal trail litter service.
waterSources: Use Berg/Kyrkviken guest harbour as the strongest confirmed public water refill point, seasonal and not in winter. Visit Möja describes container refill and harbor guides/OSM indicate limited or fee-based water, so verify current terms before relying on free access.
Jeppes may have toilet/water during opening hours for customers or fee per SAT winter/off-season notes; keep conditional, not an unconditional public tap.
Långvik/Löka/Möjaström harbour water should remain conditional boat-harbour metadata until hiker access and seasonality are verified.
Do not expose lakes, reserve water or wells/hand pumps as ordinary drinking water without later confirmation.
notes: Route shape: linear north-to-south route from Långvik to Hamn, then return to Berg for services.
Model Möja as a multi-access linear route with a return to Berg for services, not as a full loop or Möja runt.
Hamn is a route endpoint/hamlet but has no ferry quay or services according to SAT; do not create access or facility pins there.
Berg/Kyrkviken is the primary public service cluster; guest-harbour toilet/water are seasonal and not in winter.
Render ferry stops from accessMetadataDraft as the primary access layer; keep transit facilities only as fallback if the app cannot consume access metadata. Never render both layers at once.
Do not promote Dragedet, Södermöja, Granholmen or Korsö as SAT Möja trail-access quays unless a later integration supports secondary/non-SAT ferry context.
Keep Björndalen/naturstigen separate from SAT geometry unless later passes prove the SAT main route uses it. It is valuable nearby nature context but not the main gravel-road SAT section.
No official campsite is confirmed. Möja-Björndalen reserve prohibits camping; do not convert general allemansrätten context into a campsite facility.
No official public SAT fireplace/firepit is confirmed. Suppress OSM/harbour grills until public hiker use is verified.
Use opening-hours, customer/fee and booking caveats for food, lodging, showers, sauna, harbour services and restaurant/shop toilets.
Do not expose local lakes, wells or hand pumps as drinking-water facilities without later confirmation.
Treat informal bathing candidates as unmonitored unless a stronger municipal/Naturkartan source supports a specific spot; do not add HaV water-quality status unless HaV lists it.
Keep dogs controlled/leashed around wildlife, villages and protected areas; SAT states dogs must be leashed March-September and reserve rules may be stricter.
Do not import Björndalen reserve service icons as SAT facilities; the reserve is optional/local-trail context and has stricter rules than the road-based SAT section.
Do not promote wild-camping waypoints on the main island; one-off blog bivouac reports are conflict-discovery only, not sources for campsites.
